newsitem.title: THAILAND: Democrat Party seen ahead in violent Thai poll. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Democrat Party seen ahead in violent Thai poll. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]

text.p: The Democrat Party of former premier Chuan Leekpai was leading in early unofficial results in Thailand's election on Sunday, as the election watchdog reported at least seven people were shot dead in poll-related violence.
Three television stations projected that the Democrat Party was running ahead of the New Aspiration Party (NAP) headed by outgoing Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.

Their projections were based on vote-counting 90 minutes after balloting had closed at 0800 GMT. Earlier, a television station's exit poll released minutes after voting ended had put the Democrats in a dead heat with the NAP.
Channel 9 television, which had at first projected the dead heat with 124 for the NAP and the Democrats, said later that the Democrats were now set to win 136 seats against 117 for the NAP.
The election is to fill 393 seats in the lower house of parliament. A total of 2,310 candidates from 13 parties took part in the polls, seen as the closest race in memory.
In its projection, Channel 7 said the Democrats were seen winning 135 seats and the NAP 112 seats. Channel 3 put the Democrats well ahead with 129 seats to the NAP's 89.
The election, Thailand's fourth in as many years, was marred by violence and reports of bribery and intimidation, election officials said.

PollWatch, the election watchdog, said at least seven people were killed and 10 wounded in shootings related to the general election -- dubbed by analysts as the dirtiest and most violent in decades. (Corrects to clarify that shootings occurred during campaign, not all on Sunday.)
It also estimated that politicians had spent between 20 billion and 30 billion baht ($800 million and $1.2 billion) on vote-buying.
